terms.gloss: perform, carry out (a duty, a task, an office)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent; with the ablative
evidence: Phaedr. App. 19.2–3: obstetrīcis partibus sē posse fungī dīxit
terms.comment: With the ablative: officiō fungī, to do one’s duty; mūnere fungī, to hold a post and do its work (see position, a job).

evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.8: praestāre dominō sī pār officium potes
Cic. de Or. 2.38 (Lewis & Short): suum mūnus
Cic. Sen. 34 (Lewis & Short): omnia rēgis officia et mūnera

phrases.latin: premente partū scrōfa cum gemeret jacēns, accurrit lupus et obstetrīcis partibus sē posse fungī dīxit, prōmittēns opem
phrases.english: As a sow lay groaning in labour, a wolf ran up and said he could do a midwife’s part, promising help.
Let everyone do his own job.

sources: Lewis & Short: fungor · Lewis & Short: praesto · Lewis & Short: exsequor
